metadata.title: My Dead Fiancé Keeps Typing...
metadata.subtitle: Six months after his fatal crash, his chat shows "Typing..." at 1:14 AM—and he begs me to check the ravine.

nodes.text: 1:14 AM · Exactly 6 months to the minute after Liam’s car plunged off Highway 19. His archived chat bubble starts pulsing: "Typing..."
Rowan... are you awake? Don’t freak out. You have to get to Mile-Marker 19 before sunrise.
Who stole Liam’s phone?! This is sick—I’m reporting this number to the police!

nodes.transcript: [crackling, wind howling] "Our secret password is Silver Pines 09. Nobody else knows that, Rowan. Someone cut the brake line!"

nodes.text: Look at the passenger seat in the crash report. Not the driver seat.

nodes.prompt: Your hands tremble over the keyboard:

options.label: Text Detective Reyes about the crash file
options.player_reply_text: Det. Reyes, someone is texting me from Liam’s dead number knowing our secrets!

options.label: Demand Liam send a live photo right now
options.player_reply_text: If you’re really alive, send me a photo right now!

nodes.text: Det. Reyes replies: "Hold on Rowan, Liam’s phone was never recovered from the ravine—it was listed destroyed!"
Det. Reyes pings you: "Wait—my desk just got a tower alert from Mile-Marker 19! Stay home until I check!"
Another message pops up from Liam’s chat: "Reyes is lying. Why wasn’t there a closed-casket autopsy?"
The cloud sync is breaking up... dig under the guardrail at Mile-Marker 19. My spare phone is still blinking down there.
Wait... if that’s your spare phone at the ravine, then why am I holding a cracked spare phone in my own pocket?!

nodes.headline: Mile-Marker 19
nodes.teaser_text: Next: You drive through the fog to the exact crash site.

nodes.text: 1:45 AM · Thick fog swallows Highway 19. Your headlights hit the bent guardrail at Mile-Marker 19.
Rowan, your car GPS just crossed Mile-Marker 19! Turn around—it’s pitch-black and pouring rain out there!
How do you have my car’s live GPS, Detective?! I never shared that with you!

nodes.transcript: [urgent whisper] "Because someone planted a tracker on your bumper! Step over the guardrail—look for the blinking blue LED!"

nodes.text: She found the guardrail. Tell the coroner to clear the morgue logs.

nodes.prompt: Ten feet down the muddy slope, a faint blue screen glows:

options.label: Slide down and grab the glowing phone
options.player_reply_text: I got it! The screen is shattered, and it’s STILL logged into Liam’s cloud!

options.label: Screenshot Det. Reyes’s unsent message
options.player_reply_text: I caught what you just unsent about the coroner, Reyes!

nodes.text: Drop that phone and stay by the road—I’m 8 minutes away!
You’re misunderstanding—I’m trying to protect you from what’s on that phone!
You wipe mud off the cracked screen. A GPS pin pulses right beneath your boots—and a voice memo begins auto-playing.
Look at the GPS timestamp on the cracked phone, Rowan. It never stopped recording after the crash.
Wait... there’s a second car’s headlights approaching fast through the fog...

nodes.headline: Headlights in the Fog
nodes.teaser_text: Next: The cracked phone GPS pin exposes the hidden burial site.

nodes.text: 1:56 AM · You duck behind a pine tree as a black SUV slows to a crawl along the fog-choked guardrail.
Don’t let Reyes see you! Look at the GPS history on the cracked phone—he dragged someone out of the wreck at 1:20 AM!
Dragged who out?! Liam, if you survived the crash, where have you been for 6 months?!

nodes.transcript: [voice breaking, static] "I’m NOT hiding, Rowan! Check the coroner’s photo—the person buried in that grave wasn’t me!"

nodes.text: Her car is empty. Search the brush below Mile-Marker 19.

nodes.caption: Shattered phone GPS screen — signal pinned directly at Mile-Marker 19 ravine.

nodes.prompt: A flashlight beam sweeps 5 feet above your hiding spot:

options.label: Keep still and download the GPS logs
options.player_reply_text: Downloading the full GPS history to my cloud now—holding my breath.

options.label: Trigger your car panic alarm remotely
options.player_reply_text: Hit my keyfob panic button! He’s running back up to the road!

nodes.text: Transfer complete! Now look at the second pin—it’s 2 miles east at an old lakeside cabin!
Brilliant! Sprint to your car while his back is turned and head 2 miles east to the cabin!
You scramble back into your sedan and floor the gas, tires spraying gravel into the mist.
Stop driving, Rowan! If you go to that lakeside cabin, you’ll break the one thing keeping you sane!
Why are you so terrified of me seeing that cabin, Detective?!

nodes.headline: The Lakeside Cabin
nodes.teaser_text: Next: A light is burning inside the cabin at 2:15 AM.

nodes.text: 2:12 AM · You park behind the pines. Warm yellow light glows behind the cabin curtains—and a familiar silhouette crosses the window.
Wait—do NOT knock on the cabin door yet! Look through the side window first.
Oh my God... Liam is standing inside the kitchen making coffee... completely alive?!

nodes.transcript: [confused, echoing] "Wait... if I’m standing in that kitchen without a phone, then WHO has been texting you from my cloud account?!"

nodes.text: Look closely at the framed photo on his mantle.

nodes.prompt: Rain drips off the cabin eaves onto your neck:

options.label: Zoom in on the framed photo inside
options.player_reply_text: Wait... there’s a black ribbon across a framed portrait... OF ME?!

options.label: Tap on the window glass to call Liam
options.player_reply_text: I tapped the glass—Liam turned around, stared right through me, and locked the window!

nodes.text: Read the brass plaque under the photo, Rowan. November 25th—six months ago.
He didn’t ignore you—he couldn’t SEE you! Look at the framed portrait on his shelf!
Your breath doesn’t fog the cold window glass. Not a single drop of rain leaves a mark on your sleeves.
Now do you understand?! You were in the passenger seat, Rowan—and Liam paid the coroner to bury the truth!
No... I’m not dead! Wait—then why is Liam staring at his phone in terror right now?!

nodes.headline: The Framed Portrait
nodes.teaser_text: Next: Why Liam faked a death certificate—and who is really in the grave.

nodes.text: 2:24 AM · Det. Reyes’s SUV pulls into the mud beside yours. He steps out holding a waterproof evidence folder—and he DOES see you.
Wait—you’re NOT a ghost, Rowan! Liam hung a fake memorial photo to collect your $2M life insurance policy!
WHAT?! Then why did he stare right past me at the window?!

nodes.transcript: [panting, rain pounding] "Because that’s frosted one-way privacy glass! He faked YOUR death in the ravine—Wait, no, he faked HIS OWN death first, then switched the records!"

nodes.text: Someone is outside the cabin. Burn the passport.

nodes.prompt: Smoke curls from the cabin chimney:

options.label: Confront Liam on the porch with Reyes
options.player_reply_text: I’m kicking that porch door open right now—come with me, Reyes!

options.label: Block the cabin’s back exit road
options.player_reply_text: I’ll block the back trail with my car so he can’t run!

nodes.text: Hold on—back up! Liam isn’t alone inside that cabin! Someone else just handed him a duffel bag!
Wait—there’s a second car parked behind the shed! Liam has an accomplice inside!
The cabin door flies open. Liam sprints out into the rain—freezing dead in his tracks when your headlights illuminate his face.
Rowan?! I thought you—WAIT! Who has been texting you from my old number all night?!
Wait... if YOU weren’t texting me from the ravine, then who led me straight to your hideout?!

nodes.headline: Who Sent the Texts?
nodes.teaser_text: Next: The accomplice steps out of the cabin—holding the second phone.

nodes.text: 2:35 AM · Liam drops his duffel bag in the mud, hands shaking as he stares at Detective Reyes.
Rowan, RUN! Don’t get in Reyes’s SUV—HE’S the one who cut my brake line 6 months ago!
What?! Both of you stop lying! Why did Liam have a memorial photo of ME inside?!

nodes.transcript: [frantic, soaking wet] "That wasn’t a memorial—that was the forged death certificate Reyes printed to frame me! I hid here so he wouldn’t finish the job!"

nodes.text: She knows too much. Call the coroner back.

nodes.prompt: Detective Reyes slowly reaches inside his wet trench coat:

options.label: Throw your car in reverse and hit horn
options.player_reply_text: Stay back, Reyes! I’m backing out onto the main highway!

options.label: Pull Liam into your passenger seat
options.player_reply_text: Get in the car, Liam—and you better have proof in 10 seconds!

nodes.text: Liam leaps onto your hood and slides in through the passenger door: "Drive! Check the bank transfer I saved!"
Liam slams the door as gravel flies: "I have the bank wire Reyes sent the coroner—open it now!"
Your headlights vanish down the muddy trail as Reyes’s black SUV roars into pursuit behind you.
Pull over, Rowan! You’re riding with a fugitive who faked his own funeral!
Then explain the $180,000 midnight wire to the county coroner, Reyes!!

nodes.headline: Midnight Chase on 19
nodes.teaser_text: Next: The bank transfer exposes the real mastermind.

nodes.text: 2:45 AM · Tires scream around the wet curves of Highway 19. On your dashboard mount, the wire receipt loads in full.
Look at the sender routing number—that’s Reyes’s secret shell account! He paid the coroner $180,000 to declare an unidentified body as ME!
Why?! What did you ever do to Detective Reyes?!

nodes.transcript: [shouting over the engine] "I audited his precinct’s evidence fund! I found he was selling seized narcotics—so he cut my brakes and tried to steal my encrypted ledger!"

nodes.text: Don’t let them reach the state police checkpoint.

nodes.caption: Midnight wire transfer of $180,000 sent to the county coroner’s private offshore account.

nodes.prompt: Reyes’s SUV slams your rear bumper—2 miles to the state police post:

options.label: Forward the bank wire to State Police
options.player_reply_text: State Police just got the wire receipt and our live GPS—hold on!

options.label: Broadcast the proof live to local news
options.player_reply_text: Uploaded the wire transfer and audio to the state prosecutor AND newsroom!

nodes.text: Red and blue barricades ahead! State troopers are stepping out onto the highway!
Reyes’s phone just exploded with internal-affairs alerts—he’s swerving off the shoulder!
Three state police cruisers box in the black SUV with spike strips as you skid safely behind the barricade.
Internal Affairs just cuffed Reyes and froze the coroner’s offshore account! Wait—Liam, why did you stop breathing for a second?
Wait... the state trooper just walked up to my window and asked: "Ma’am, why are you talking to an empty passenger seat?"

nodes.headline: The Empty Passenger Seat
nodes.teaser_text: Next: The most chilling twist of the night hits like ice water.

nodes.text: 2:56 AM · You whip your head to the right. The passenger seat is dry, spotless, and completely empty—except for the shattered phone from the ravine.
I’m sorry I couldn’t tell you until Reyes was in cuffs, Rowan. I really didn’t survive the ravine 6 months ago.
No... I saw you in the cabin! You jumped into my car! You handed me the wire receipt!

nodes.transcript: [warm, fading into static] "I hid that wire receipt on my spare phone before the brakes failed. I only stayed long enough to make sure Reyes didn’t silence you next."

nodes.text: The cabin has been abandoned since November.

nodes.prompt: The state trooper knocks gently on your window:

options.label: Hand the cracked phone to the trooper
options.player_reply_text: Officer, everything you need to convict Reyes is on this cracked phone.

options.label: Save Liam’s last voice note first
options.player_reply_text: Saved your voice note forever, Liam. Handing the phone to the police now.

nodes.text: The trooper looks at the shattered screen—somehow still displaying the bank transfer clearly—and nods solemnly.
The moment your download finishes, the cracked screen goes black for good.
In the rearview mirror, Reyes screams from the back of the cruiser as Internal Affairs reads the murder and bribery charges.
One last line flickers across your chat before "Typing..." vanishes forever: "Live a long, fearless life for both of us."
Goodbye, Liam... justice is finally yours.

nodes.headline: Stopped Typing Forever
nodes.teaser_text: Finale next: Dawn breaks over Mile-Marker 19.

nodes.text: 6:14 AM · Morning mist lifts off Highway 19. You lay a bouquet of white lilies beside the repaired guardrail.
Archive System: "Chat thread with Liam permanently locked — Account closed."
They arrested the coroner this morning too. Everyone who hurt you is going away for life.

nodes.transcript: [replaying your saved clip—warm smile in his voice] "Silver Pines 09. Remember I’m always in your corner, Rowan."

nodes.text: No more 1:14 AM nightmares.

options.label: Lock your phone and smile through tears
options.player_reply_text: Thank you for saving me one last time.

options.label: Leave your spare keychain by the lilies
options.player_reply_text: Leaving the matching Silver Pines keychain right here with you.

nodes.text: A gentle mountain breeze lifts the petals of the white lilies into the golden morning light.
The silver keychain glints softly in the sunrise—never forgotten.
You step back into your car and drive toward the sunrise, leaving Mile-Marker 19 in peace.
Final status: Case solved. Coroner and Det. Reyes indicted on all counts.
He kept typing just long enough to save my life.

nodes.headline: Rest in Peace, Liam
nodes.teaser_text: You finished "My Dead Fiancé Keeps Typing..."! Explore more mind-bending stories.
